content.introduction: The Student Portal is your central hub for managing all aspects of your academic life. From registration to grades, everything you need is accessible in one place.

sections.title: Getting Started
sections.content:
Accessing the Portal:
1. Enter your university username (your email prefix)
2. Enter your password
3. Complete two-factor authentication if enabled

First-time users should activate their account through the link sent to their personal email after admission.

sections.title: Registration
sections.content:
Course Registration:
- View available courses by term
- Search by subject, instructor, or time
- Add courses to your shopping cart
- Submit registration when your enrollment window opens
- Drop or swap courses before deadlines

Registration Windows:
- Seniors: First week of registration
- Juniors: Second week
- Sophomores: Third week
- Freshmen: Fourth week

sections.title: Academic Records
sections.content:
View Your Records:
- Current and past grades
- Unofficial transcript
- Degree audit and progress
- GPA calculator
- Academic standing

Order Official Documents:
- Official transcripts ($10 each)
- Enrollment verification letters
- Degree verification

sections.title: Financial Information
sections.content:
Access Financial Services:
- View tuition and fees
- Check financial aid awards
- Make payments online
- Set up payment plans
- View 1098-T tax forms
- Direct deposit enrollment for refunds

sections.title: Personal Settings
sections.content:
Manage Your Account:
- Update contact information
- Change password
- Set up emergency contacts
- Update privacy settings (FERPA)
- Manage notification preferences
- Upload profile photo for ID card

content.conclusion: Check the portal regularly for important announcements, holds on your account, and upcoming deadlines. Enable notifications to stay informed.

content.introduction: The Course Catalog is your comprehensive guide to all courses offered at the university, including descriptions, prerequisites, and degree requirements.

sections.title: Navigating the Catalog
sections.content:
Finding Courses:
- Browse by department or subject area
- Search by course number or keyword
- Filter by level (100-400 level)
- View by term availability

Course Information Includes:
- Course number and title
- Credit hours
- Description of content
- Prerequisites and corequisites
- Typical offering pattern (Fall, Spring, etc.)

sections.title: Understanding Course Numbers
sections.content:
Course Level Guide:
- 100-199: Introductory courses for freshmen
- 200-299: Intermediate courses for sophomores
- 300-399: Advanced courses for juniors/seniors
- 400-499: Senior-level and capstone courses
- 500+: Graduate-level courses

Course Prefixes:
- Each department has a unique prefix (e.g., MATH, ENGL, BIOL)
- Cross-listed courses appear under multiple prefixes

sections.title: Degree Requirements
sections.content:
General Education:
- Writing and Communication: 6 credits
- Mathematics: 3-6 credits
- Natural Sciences: 6-8 credits
- Social Sciences: 6 credits
- Humanities: 6 credits
- Diversity: 3 credits

Major Requirements:
- Core courses required for all majors
- Electives within the major
- Capstone or senior project
- Minimum GPA requirements

sections.title: Special Course Types
sections.content:
Independent Study:
- Work one-on-one with faculty
- Design your own research project
- Requires faculty sponsor and approval

Internship Credits:
- Earn credit for work experience
- Must be pre-approved
- Requires learning agreement

Study Abroad:
- Transfer credits from approved programs
- May fulfill major or general education requirements
- Pre-approval required

content.conclusion: Always verify current requirements with your academic advisor. Catalog requirements may change, but you follow the catalog from your entry year.

content.introduction: The university library provides extensive resources to support your academic research, including databases, e-journals, physical collections, and expert assistance.

sections.title: Online Databases
sections.content:
Research Databases:
- JSTOR: Humanities and social sciences
- PubMed: Medical and life sciences
- IEEE Xplore: Engineering and technology
- ProQuest: Dissertations and newspapers
- Web of Science: Multidisciplinary research
- EBSCOhost: Business and general research

Access:
- Log in with your university credentials
- Available 24/7 from any location
- Off-campus access through VPN or proxy

sections.title: Finding Materials
sections.content:
Library Catalog:
- Search for books, journals, and media
- Check availability and location
- Place holds on checked-out items
- Request interlibrary loans

Research Guides:
- Subject-specific guides by librarians
- Recommended databases for each field
- Citation guides and tutorials
- Assignment-specific resources

sections.title: Library Services
sections.content:
Borrowing:
- Undergraduates: 4 weeks loan period
- Graduate students: Semester loan
- Renewals available online
- Overdue fines: $0.25/day

Research Help:
- Reference desk assistance
- Research consultations (schedule at front desk)
- Chat and email reference
- Subject librarians for in-depth help

sections.title: Study Spaces
sections.content:
Individual Study:
- Quiet floors (3rd and 4th)
- Study carrels
- Computer workstations

Group Study:
- Reservable study rooms
- Collaborative spaces
- Whiteboard rooms

Hours:
- Regular: Mon-Thu 7AM-12AM, Fri 7AM-9PM, Sat 9AM-9PM, Sun 10AM-12AM
- Extended hours during finals

sections.title: Technology Resources
sections.content:
Available Equipment:
- Laptop lending (4-hour in-library use)
- Chargers and adapters
- Headphones
- Calculators
- Presentation equipment

Printing and Scanning:
- Print stations on every floor
- Free scanning to email
- Color and large format printing

content.conclusion: Librarians are here to help! Don't hesitate to ask for assistance with your research. Schedule a consultation for complex projects.

content.introduction: The Tutoring Center provides free academic support to help you succeed in your courses. Our trained tutors can assist with a wide range of subjects.

sections.title: Services Offered
sections.content:
Individual Tutoring:
- One-on-one sessions with trained tutors
- 30-60 minute appointments
- Scheduled or drop-in availability

Group Tutoring:
- Study groups for specific courses
- Collaborative learning environment
- Regular weekly sessions

Supplemental Instruction:
- Attached to high-challenge courses
- Weekly review sessions
- Led by students who excelled in the course

sections.title: Subjects Available
sections.content:
Mathematics:
- Algebra through Calculus III
- Statistics and Probability
- Linear Algebra
- Differential Equations

Sciences:
- Biology and Chemistry
- Physics
- Computer Science

Writing:
- Essay development
- Research papers
- Lab reports
- Citation help

Other Subjects:
- Economics
- Accounting
- Foreign Languages
- Check at front desk for full list

sections.title: How to Schedule
sections.content:
Online Booking:
1. Log into the tutoring portal
2. Select your subject
3. Choose available time slot
4. Receive confirmation email

Drop-In Hours:
- Math Lab: Mon-Thu 10AM-6PM
- Writing Center: Mon-Fri 9AM-5PM
- Science Help: Tue/Thu 2-6PM

Location: Learning Commons, Library 2nd Floor

sections.title: Tips for Success
sections.content:
Before Your Session:
- Identify specific questions or problems
- Bring your textbook and notes
- Attempt problems before asking for help
- Review relevant class material

During Your Session:
- Be an active participant
- Ask questions and take notes
- Work through problems, don't just watch
- Be honest about what you don't understand

content.conclusion: Tutoring is most effective when used regularly, not just before exams. Visit early and often for the best results!

content.introduction: The Writing Center helps students at all levels improve their writing skills. We work with you on any type of writing, at any stage of the process.

sections.title: Our Services
sections.content:
We Help With:
- Essays and research papers
- Lab reports and technical writing
- Creative writing
- Personal statements and applications
- Resumes and cover letters
- Thesis and dissertation work

All Stages Welcome:
- Brainstorming and outlining
- Drafting and revising
- Editing and polishing
- Citation and formatting

sections.title: How Sessions Work
sections.content:
What to Expect:
- 30-50 minute sessions
- Collaborative conversation about your writing
- Focus on your priorities and concerns
- Learn strategies you can apply later

What We Don't Do:
- Proofread or edit for you
- Write or rewrite your paper
- Guarantee a specific grade

Our Philosophy:
- Writers learn best by doing
- We teach skills, not quick fixes
- Every writer can improve

sections.title: Scheduling
sections.content:
Appointments:
- Book at the front desk or by phone
- Available 7 days a week
- In-person and online options

Drop-In Hours:
- Sunday-Thursday: 7-10 PM
- First come, first served
- 20-minute sessions

Location: Library Room 204

sections.title: Preparing for Your Visit
sections.content:
Bring:
- Your assignment instructions
- Any drafts or outlines
- Notes from class
- Specific questions or concerns

Before You Come:
- Review your assignment carefully
- Make notes on what's confusing you
- Try writing something, even if rough

content.conclusion: Good writing takes practice and feedback. Visit us regularly to develop your skills throughout your academic career.

content.introduction: Study abroad offers life-changing opportunities to learn in a new culture, gain global perspective, and grow personally and professionally.

sections.title: Program Types
sections.content:
Semester/Year Programs:
- Full immersion experience
- Take courses at partner universities
- Live with local students or families
- Duration: 4-12 months

Summer Programs:
- Intensive 4-8 week programs
- Faculty-led or independent
- Earn 3-9 credits

Short-Term Programs:
- Winter or spring break trips
- 1-3 weeks
- Faculty-led with classmates

Internships Abroad:
- Gain international work experience
- Available in many fields
- Credit-bearing options

sections.title: Popular Destinations
sections.content:
Europe:
- United Kingdom, Spain, France
- Italy, Germany, Ireland

Asia:
- Japan, China, South Korea
- Australia, New Zealand

Americas:
- Costa Rica, Argentina, Chile
- Canada, Mexico

Africa & Middle East:
- South Africa, Morocco
- Israel, Jordan

sections.title: How to Apply
sections.content:
Timeline:
- Research programs: 12+ months before
- Apply: 6-9 months before departure
- Deadlines: October 1 (spring), March 1 (fall/summer)

Application Requirements:
- Minimum 2.5 GPA (some programs higher)
- Sophomore standing or above
- Application essay
- Faculty recommendation
- Interview (some programs)

sections.title: Costs and Financial Aid
sections.content:
What's Typically Included:
- Tuition at host institution
- Housing
- Some meals
- Excursions and activities

Additional Costs:
- Airfare
- Passport and visa fees
- Personal spending
- Travel insurance

Financial Aid:
- Most aid applies to approved programs
- Study abroad scholarships available
- Payment plans accepted

sections.title: Academic Credit
sections.content:
Credit Transfer:
- Courses must be pre-approved
- Fill out course equivalency form
- Work with your advisor early

Degree Progress:
- Can fulfill major requirements
- General education credits
- Elective credits
- Grades transfer as pass/fail or letter (varies)

content.conclusion: Start planning early! Visit the Study Abroad Office in the International Center to explore your options and begin the application process.
